_note: Margaret Atwood's own words only, each checked verbatim against the page in 'checked_url' (the page the wording was matched on; 'primary_source' when that differs from the listed 'url') on 2026-10-23.

_verification.method: Verbatim check on 2026-10-23: every source page was downloaded as raw HTML/PDF (Wayback Machine snapshot where the live site refuses non-browser requests) and each quote's text was string-matched against the page text, ignoring only quote-mark/dash typography. Aggregator pages (Goodreads, Wikiquote, quote listicles) were also searched for a primary source; quotes found only on aggregators are verified=false.
_verification.fields: per quote: verified, checked_url (page the wording was matched on), primary_source (when not the listed url), note, was (original text when corrected)
_verification.rule: Only quotes with verified=true and without excluded_from_game may be used in game (tests/test_quotes_vv.gd).

_speech_habits.what: Margaret Atwood's own recurring phrases and verbal habits, as she actually said them in recorded talks: the dry, flat, digressive lecture delivery the cruise plays for laughs. Every entry is verbatim from a recording; nothing is paraphrased or invented.
_speech_habits.method: 2026-10-23: audio downloaded with yt-dlp (kept outside the repo); faster-whisper small.en transcribed each whole talk with word timestamps; each candidate utterance was located in those word timestamps and its span (+/-0.8 s) re-transcribed independently with faster-whisper medium.en. verified=true only when both passes give the same words (ignoring punctuation and case); where they disagree the entry is verified=false and the note quotes what medium.en heard. Resemblyzer speaker similarity against the Atwood reference clips is recorded in each note. In the Texas Book Festival conversation only lines that are Atwood's own turns were taken.
_speech_habits.fields: per entry: text, habit (group label), source, url, timestamp (m:ss-m:ss in the recording at url), aggregator, verified, checked_url, note; fragment=true marks a tag or clause that only shows the habit and is not a whole line; excluded_from_game as in quotes.
_speech_habits.rule: Only entries with verified=true and without fragment or excluded_from_game may be spoken in game (tools/export_voice_lines.py voices exactly those).

recurring.like that (sentence tag): ends a description with a flat 'like that' (MIT lecture 1x, Texas 2009 3x)
recurring.cheer: calls her own bleak books cheering/cheerful/cheerier (MIT 5x, Texas 5x: transcript word count)
recurring.anyway: 'Anyway,' to drop a digression and start another (MIT 6x, Texas 2x)
recurring.that is, (restating): restates the sentence she just said, starting 'That is,' (MIT 5x)
recurring.first of all / number one: enumerates even small points (MIT 3x 'first of all', 2x 'number one'; Texas 1x)
recurring.and so forth / et cetera: trails lists off (MIT 2x 'and so forth', 1x each 'et cetera')
recurring.this is true: vouches flatly for an absurd anecdote ('This is a true story', 'Now I do not lie, this is true': MIT 3x)
recurring.let me ask you / if I were them: turns a question back on the asker; gives advice as 'If I were them, I would...' (Texas 2x each)
recurring.handling questions: repeats and reformulates the question, then 'What was the question?' / 'Anything else you'd like to know?'
